title: Wren and the Typewriter
premise: Ines Dunmore, a mapmaker's apprentice hiding under the alias 'Wren,' is finishing the atlas her late master died protecting when winter closes the mountain bridge and seals the valley town of Corvane until spring. A government surveyor arrives with orders to confiscate the master's maps — and news that one berth remains on the last mail coach out before the pass avalanches. As Ines races to complete the atlas and conceal her true identity, she must decide whether to give the berth to Tam, the printer's boy who has become her brother in everything but blood, or to Marisol, the typist who knows who Ines really is and holds the letters that could save or destroy her. In the end, Ines gives up the berth herself, sends the finished atlas out under both their names, and chooses truth over invisibility — staying in Corvane as the snow falls, finally at home.
about_author: Paloma Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing cartographic collections in alpine monasteries before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about quiet people caught in loud histories, and lives where the roads close every winter by choice.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Ines, working secretly as 'Wren' in the dead mapmaker Aldous Dunmore's cluttered studio, inks the final coastal plates of his forbidden atlas while the town prepares for winter. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; she touches the unfinished page and promises him she'll finish it.

chapters.title: Last Cart Across
chapters.summary: The bridge closes with a ceremonial chaining of the gates; Ines watches the last carts cross and feels the trap of the season settle. Tam, the printer's apprentice, drags her to the harvest feast where she almost enjoys belonging. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by dread — visibility is danger.

chapters.title: A Man with Official Ink
chapters.summary: Surveyor Elias Brand arrives on foot ahead of the snow, carrying warrants for Dunmore's 'seditious' maps and requisitioning lodging at the studio itself. He notices Wren's steady hand and asks too many questions. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into vigilance; the atlas must be hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: Marisol's Drawer
chapters.summary: Ines discovers that Marisol, the postmistress-typist, keeps a drawer of undelivered letters — including ones addressed to Ines's real name from a family she fled years ago. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two keepers of secrets recognizing each other across a counter.

chapters.title: What Tam Saw
chapters.summary: Tam catches Ines burning a draft plate and demands the truth; she gives him half of it. Meanwhile Brand offers Tam a chance to inform in exchange for passage off the mountain. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by temptation and hurt at being kept outside her confidence.

chapters.title: The Berth
chapters.summary: Brand announces the mail coach will make one final run before the pass closes — one passenger seat, priority given to those with official business. The whole town angles for it; Ines realizes the atlas can leave only if someone carries it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: hope curdling into an impossible arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: Snow on the Copper Plates
chapters.summary: Working through a whiteout week, Ines finishes the atlas's final sheet — a map of Corvane itself, drawn with a tenderness she never gave any coastline. Brand nearly discovers the plates hidden inside the printing press. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the work becomes a love letter to the place she claimed not to belong to.

chapters.title: Letters, Delivered Late
chapters.summary: Marisol, moved by Ines's choice, hands over the old letters: her family wrote not to condemn her but to say they understood why she left. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving years late; identity reframed as something chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: The Coach Bell
chapters.summary: Climax: at the gate, Ines puts Tam on the coach with the atlas sewn into his coat, refusing Brand's bargain and confessing her identity publicly to buy Tam safe passage. Brand lets them go — he wanted the maps finished, not burned. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-definition; the lie dies so the truth can travel.

chapters.title: Spring, Eventually
chapters.summary: Resolution: winter passes; Ines stays in Corvane with Marisol and the town that now knows her name. When the bridge reopens, a package arrives — the published atlas, credited to 'Wren Dunmore,' with a letter from Tam. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet joy; found family confirmed, invisibility voluntarily surrendered.
